meta.title: Computer Vision for Product Data Collection in Industrial Ecology
meta.subtitle: A taxonomy of CV applications, mapped to physical scale and information type
meta.source: Paper 2 (JIE Review), Table S1 + Table S2. Verdicts are the paper's; do not alter without changing the draft.

maturityLevels.gloss: Mature, well-benchmarked, deployable within a stated caveat.
Exists but needs tuning or verification, or degrades out of domain.
maturityLevels.handling: Human-in-the-loop verify every field; propagate elevated uncertainty; flag EoL-degraded capture.

maturityLevels.gloss: Works only inside the narrow object class it was built for; generalization fails across classes.
maturityLevels.handling: Treat as unavailable for arbitrary products; do not populate.

maturityLevels.gloss: In principle possible, no validation under realistic capture.
maturityLevels.handling: Do not populate an inventory field; retain as human-authored, redundancy-checked (k-of-n).

maturityLevels.gloss: No method maps to the cell; out of scope for direct capture.

product.name: End-of-life desk fan
product.note: Representative multi-component WEEE product chosen for the visualization; the taxonomy is product-general (the paper's Table S2 walks a laptop through the same cells).

cells.methodFamily: OCR + database matching; retrieval / one-shot recognition
cells.maturityNote: Validated and deployed in-domain, but degrades materially under EoL capture: label read 95.7% repair -> 90.8% reuse -> 39.7% recycle.
cells.failureMode: EoL label degradation (damaged, dirty, skewed, distant); database coverage; not autonomous (human-in-the-loop selection).
cells.example: Washing-machine label reading run by non-experts on commodity phones (Sterkens et al. 2023).

cells.methodFamily: Monocular metric depth; feed-forward multi-view geometry; (generation-based 3D = documentation only)
cells.maturityNote: Geometry approximate, observed; depth/multi-view benchmarked on general scenes, not EoL products. Weight an approximate quantity, not a measurement; generation-based 3D is not measurement.
cells.failureMode: Visible-surface only; residual scale sensitivity to capture metadata; weight compounds geometry x material error.
cells.example: Single-image mass estimation (Standley et al. 2017; Wang et al. 2026).

cells.maturityNote: Structurally empty: structure is resolved at the component scale. m = d (derived/unmapped); carries no row in Table S1.

cells.task: Wear / damage; repair / reuse / recycle triage
cells.methodFamily: Supervised defect detection; zero-shot anomaly detection (WinCLIP / AnomalyCLIP); VLM description; triage = value/material sorting
cells.failureMode: No validation under realistic capture; triage today is value/material sorting, not per-unit grading.
cells.example: Exterior vehicle damage assessment (Hasan et al. 2025).

cells.maturityNote: Naming feasible; fine-grained part identity not reliable; out-of-domain weak (15.7 mAP multi-domain).
cells.failureMode: Missing/degraded markings; out-of-domain weakness of zero-shot recognition.
cells.example: Open-vocabulary detection (Liu et al. 2025, Grounding DINO).

cells.methodFamily: Monocular metric depth; feed-forward multi-view geometry
cells.failureMode: Occlusion within assembly aggravates visible-surface limit; scale sensitivity.
cells.example: Single-image / multi-view geometry (Hu et al. 2024, Metric3D v2; Wang et al. 2025, VGGT).

cells.task: Detection, segmentation, counting, attachment relations (Bill of Components)
cells.methodFamily: Closed-set / open-set detection; foundation segmentation + class-assignment; (image -> articulation for relations)
cells.maturityNote: Detect/segment Partial (~98.8% mAP50 on a narrow benchmark, needs domain tuning). BoC relations Emerging-but-narrow (graph-topology accuracy ~82% in-domain -> ~39% out-of-distribution).
cells.rubricMarks: detect/seg: i ✓ · ii ✗ᵃ · iii ~ · m s;  relations: i ✗ · ii ✗ᵃ · iii ✗ · m n
cells.failureMode: Out-of-domain and zero-shot weakness (needs domain adaptation + class-assignment layer); no general attachment graph.
cells.example: E-waste / laptop teardown segmentation (Zhang et al. 2026); image -> articulation (Liu 2025 SINGAPO; Chen 2024 URDFormer; Yuan 2025 LARM).

cells.methodFamily: Supervised defect detection; connector-state (requirements only); embodied/VLA (immature)
cells.maturityNote: Plausible-but-unvalidated; connector-state absent (requirements only); centralized-cell-bound where demonstrated.
cells.hardware: Server- and cell-bound for demonstrated capability
cells.failureMode: No validated decentralized per-unit grading; embodied disassembly unreliable (0/20 unaided).
cells.example: Robotic disassembly cells (Liu et al. 2025, RAISE; Liu et al. 2025, VLA selective disassembly).

cells.task: Surface and subsurface material ID (Bill of Materials)
cells.methodFamily: RGB classification (controlled); one/few-shot similarity (needs mask); few-shot VLM; dense surface segmentation
cells.maturityNote: Surface-region ID, controlled conditions only; no per-component quantified or occluded BoM. The one deployed image-based material-ID precedent (a shredded-WEEE sorter) characterizes a de-identified aggregate stream, not a per-unit intact product, so no per-unit deployed precedent exists (axis iii ✗).
cells.failureMode: Domain shift (100% -> ~0% under lighting/angle shift); multi-material label compositeness (~90% TrashNet -> ~40% MultiWaste); clutter in realistic scenes.
cells.example: Controlled RGB material classification (Penumuru et al. 2020); few-shot VLM material recognition (Funk et al. 2026); 3D surface material segmentation (Li 2024 MaterialSeg3D; Drehwald 2023).

cells.methodFamily: Derived: component geometry x material class x density prior
cells.maturityNote: Absent as a standalone method; compounds geometry + identity uncertainty. m = d (derived).
cells.failureMode: Compounds both inputs; no image -> BoM supply.

cells.maturityNote: Structurally empty: structure is resolved at the component scale. m = d (derived/unmapped); carries no row in Table S1.

cells.failureMode: Domain shift; clutter; no validated per-region condition grading.
cells.example: Surface / particle segmentation (Li et al. 2024, MaterialSeg3D).
